~50% of ERCOT existing gas-CC fleet contractable (EIA-860 2024 operable NG combined cycle: TX ~48 GW nameplate, ~40 GW in ERCOT), mirroring the nuclear_existing 50%-of-fleet logic (ADR 0009/0012). Strong CO2 geology: Gulf Coast saline formations, existing CO2 pipeline network, active TX Class VI queue.
Generous new-build headroom: best-in-US CO2 storage (Gulf Coast saline + EOR offtake), gas supply at Waha discount, fast ERCOT interconnection (ADR 0012).

~50% of CAISO existing gas-CC fleet (EIA-860 2024: CA ~23 GW NG-CC nameplate, ~17 GW in CAISO after LADWP/BANC munis). Central Valley saline storage exists (CTV/Class VI applications) but CEQA/CARB permitting slows deployment.
Moderate: Central Valley saline basins support storage, but new gas-burning capacity faces SB 100/CARB headwinds - cap reflects policy more than geology (ADR 0012).

~50% of PJM existing gas-CC fleet (EIA-860 2024: PA+NJ+MD+DE+WV+VA+OH ~55 GW NG-CC nameplate, nearly all PJM). Appalachian/Illinois-basin storage on the western footprint; eastern-seaboard CCs would need CO2 pipelines west.
Solid: cheap Marcellus/Utica gas, Appalachian + Illinois basin storage on the western footprint; eastern PJM thinner geology tempers the cap (ADR 0012).

~50% of MISO existing gas-CC fleet (EIA-860 2024: MISO-footprint states ~40 GW NG-CC nameplate after non-MISO shares of LA/MO/TX-border fleets). Strong geology: Illinois Basin (Decatur demonstration) north, Gulf Coast saline in MISO South.
Generous: Illinois Basin + Gulf Coast (MISO South) CO2 storage, near-hub gas, large industrial CO2-hub momentum (ADR 0012).

Fleet-share basis would be ~6,000 MW (50% of NY ~11.7 GW NG-CC, EIA-860 2024) but NY has essentially no in-state Class VI saline storage or CO2 pipelines - captured CO2 must move interstate (PA/OH), so the cap is geology-derated well below fleet share (ADR 0012).
Thin: no in-state storage geology, CLCPA hostile to new gas; nonzero only via interstate CO2 transport (ADR 0012).

Fleet-share basis would be ~7,200 MW (50% of New England ~14.4 GW NG-CC, EIA-860 2024) but New England has no viable onshore CO2 storage basin and no CO2 pipelines; only long-haul transport or offshore storage could serve it, so the cap is geology-derated furthest (ADR 0012).
Thinnest US CO2 storage geology + winter-constrained gas (Algonquin) - small cap reflects both (ADR 0012).
